subject: Shaders
suitability: Motion and procedural design reference; GPU effects library with a visual editor.

observations: GPU effects are composed as layers and rendered on WebGPU.
Documented uses include textures, shape materials, distortions, image stylization, cursor effects, blurs and transitions.
Bindings cover React, Vue, Svelte, Solid and JavaScript; Framer integration is also available.
Without WebGPU the canvas remains transparent.
Effects can modify preceding layers or only their nested children.
The documented example combines a moving color field, a grid and distortion.
The official index separates textures, shapes, shape effects, stylize, interactive, distortions, transitions, blurs and adjustments.
Marketing and documentation component totals differ; no exact asset count is inferred.
Open-source engine, components, bindings and CLI use MIT.
The editor service and curated Free/Pro presets, collections and sections have separate conditions.
The Content license restricts redistribution as libraries, templates, downloadable packages or competing design services.
Official public software repository is linked by the website.
Its pinned LICENSE is stored separately; no software package is installed or executed.

rightsDecision: Store a discovery reference with independent Motion Lab illustration. Do not mirror any curated preset or editor export. MIT software rights do not cover the hosted preset catalog.
existingOverlap: No existing catalog or preserved variant uses the shaders.com hostname. ShaderGradient and Shadertoy are different projects.
previewScope: Independent SVG explanation of input layers, shape masking and composited distortion; no WGSL execution or source-frame fidelity.
